summary.text: Cindy Holscher is the Democratic nominee for governor of Kansas and a state senator from Overland Park, first elected to the Senate in 2020 after serving in the Kansas House. Her campaign centers on school funding, health care access, cutting property taxes by lowering assessment rates, a pause on new data centers, and legalizing cannabis.

paragraphs.text: Holscher was born in Slater, Missouri, and grew up on a farm, the daughter of a union construction worker and an elementary school employee.
She was a first-generation college graduate, earning degrees in journalism and political science from the University of Missouri in 1992.
She spent most of her career before office at Sprint and also worked as a substitute teacher; her campaign says it was concern for Kansas schools that led her into public service.
She and her husband, Greg, have lived in Kansas for over 25 years and have three children.
Holscher served in the Kansas House from 2017 to 2020, where she co-founded the Women's Bipartisan Caucus.
She won a seat in the Kansas Senate in 2020 and has represented District 8 since 2021.
She won the 2026 Democratic primary for governor over fellow state Sen. Ethan Corson and chose Rep. KC Ohaebosim as her running mate.
